'''Michael Nosonovsky''' (born 1969) is a professor of [[mechanical engineering]] at the [[University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee]] known for his contribution to [[Tribology]], [[Surface science]], and [[Hebrew]] [[Epigraphy]].

== Education and career ==
Nosonovsky graduated from [[St. Petersburg Polytechnic University]] with a MSc degree in Mechanics / Mechanical Engineering in 1992.<ref>[https://gefter.ru/archive/15193 “Everything you wanted to know about an American Professor but were afraid to ask" (Russian)]</ref> In 1989-1993 he was a student of [[St. Petersburg Institute of Jewish Studies|St. Petersburg Jewish University]], of which he became the first alumnus and where he worked as a teacher of Hebrew from 1992 till 1997.<ref>{{cite book | author1 = Goldin, S. |title=Becoming Post-Communist |chapter=Becoming Jews: The Petersburg Jewish University in the 1990s |doi=10.1093/oso/9780197687215.003.0008 | year = 2023 | pages = 139–162 | isbn = 978-0-19-768721-5 }}</ref> In 2001, he got PhD degree in Mechanical Engineering from [[Northeastern University]] in [[Boston]], advisor [[George G. Adams (engineer)|George Adams]].<ref>[https://coe.northeastern.edu/people/adams-george/ George Adams' Graduate Students]</ref> He was a postdoctoral scholar at [[Ohio State University]] (2002-2005, advisor [[Bharat Bhushan (academic)|Bharat Bhushan]]<ref>[https://www.cnr.it/sigla/genericdownload/cv-bhushan-oscurato.pdf?nodeRef=workspace://SpacesStore/07e46ee8-2071-4a54-8f8a-a0f7db8bf51a Bharat Bhushan's Visiting Scientists]</ref>), [[National Institute of Standards and Technology]] (2005-2007), and [[Stevens Institute of Technology]] (2007-2009).

Since 2009, he has been a professor of Mechanical Engineering at the [[University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee]]. Since 2016, he is a Fellow of the [[American Society of Mechanical Engineers]].<ref> [https://www.asme.org/getmedia/fb97cd75-1c6c-42be-be8b-5b1bc78f6959/fellows-all-updated-june-2025_3.pdf ASME Fellows]</ref>
Nosonovsky was a visiting professor or fellow at the [[Hebrew University]] (2016), the [[Technion]] (2017), [[University of Tyumen]] (2017-2023), [[ITMO University]] (2021-2025),<ref>[https://news.itmo.ru/en/science/life_science/news/12307/ ITMO Fellowship Stories: Prof. Michael Nosonovsky on Triboinformatics, Working Across an Ocean, and Latin Dance]</ref> [[Ariel University]] (2024) and [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] (2024).<ref>[https://sites.uwm.edu/nosonovs/cv/ Prof. Nosonovsky's Curriculum Vitæ]</ref>

== Research ==
Nosonovsky's research interests include [[Tribology]], [[Contact mechanics]], surface science and engineering, and interfacial phenomena such as droplets and bubbles.<ref>[https://uwm.edu/news/super-surfaces-suggested-by-nature/ L. Otto "Super-surfaces suggested by nature"]</ref> He predicted theoretically [[Friction#Dry friction and instabilities|Adams-Martins instabilities]] during the contact of rough periodic elastic surfaces<ref>{{cite journal | author1 = Nosonovsky, M. | author2 = Adams, G. G. | title = Vibration and stability of frictional sliding of two elastic bodies with a wavy contact interface |doi=10.1115/1.1653684| journal = Journal of Applied Mechanics| year = 2004| volume = 71| issue = 2 | pages = 154–161 | bibcode = 2004JAM....71..154N }}</ref> and extended the studies of mechanical frictional instabilities to a broad class of interfacial chemical and physical phenomena.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Nosonovsky |first1=M. |last2=Mortazavi |first2=V. |date=2014 |title=Friction-Induced Vibrations and Self-Organization |url=https://www.routledge.com/Friction-Induced-Vibrations-and-Self-Organization-Mechanics-and-Non-Equilibrium/Nosonovsky-Mortazavi/p/book/9781466504011 |location=Boca Raton, FL |publisher=CRC Press |isbn=978-1-1380-7432-3}}</ref> 

At [[Ohio State University]], he studied the scale effect on friction, which is used in various areas, including the magnetic disk industry.<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/2005/01/27/technology/circuits/on-the-road-to-lowfriction-micro-devices-some-bumps.html Ian Austen, “On the Road to Low-Friction Micro Devices, Some Bumps” (New York Times, January 27, 2005)]</ref>  After that, Nosonovsky investigated the role of multi-scale and hierarchical structures on solid surfaces and demonstrated that such structures enhance the stability of superhydrophobic biomimetic [[Lotus effect]] surfaces,<ref>{{cite journal | author1 = Nosonovsky, M. | title = Multiscale roughness and stability of superhydrophobic biomimetic interfaces |doi=10.1021/la062301d| journal = Langmuir| year = 2007| volume = 23| issue = 6 | pages = 3157–3161 | pmid = 17295522 }}</ref> which, according to [[New Scientist]], was a "game changing result" that could be utilized in the design of non-sticky materials.<ref>{{cite journal | author1 = Griggs, Jessica | title = Omniphobia: the stuffs that stick at nothing |doi=10.1016/S0262-4079(12)63021-8| journal = New Scientist| year = 2012| volume = 216| issue = 2892 | pages = 46–49 | bibcode = 2012NewSc.216...46G }}</ref> He also proposed a new classification of superhydrophobic surfaces based on the multiscale roughness with account to the "rose petal effect".<ref>{{cite journal | author1 = Bhushan, B. | author2 = Nosonovsky, M. | title = The rose petal effect and the modes of superhydrophobicity |doi=10.1098/rsta.2010.0203| journal = Phil. Trans. Royal Soc. A| year = 2010| volume = 368| issue = 1929 | pages = 4713–4728 | pmid = 20855317 | bibcode = 2010RSPTA.368.4713B }}</ref> Nosonovsky suggested a procedure to derive the Amontons-Coulomb law of dry friction from the [[Second law of thermodynamics]] using [[Non-equilibrium thermodynamics]] and a limiting transition from a 3D (bulk) to a 2D (surface) material description.<ref>{{cite journal | author1 = Nosonovsky, M. | title = Entropy in Tribology: in Search for Applications |doi=10.3390/e12061345| journal = Entropy| year = 2010| volume = 12| issue = 6 | pages = 1345–1390 | doi-access = free }}</ref> With colleagues in [[NIST]], he studied water under tension (negative pressure) in microscopic capillary bridges using the [[Atomic force microscopy]] and reported negative pressure (tensile stress) reaching −160 MPa,<ref>{{cite journal | author1 = Yang. S.H. | author2 = Nosonovsky, M. | author3 = Zhang, H. | author4 = Chung, K.H. | title = Nanoscale water capillary bridges under deeply negative pressure |doi=10.1016/j.cplett.2007.11.068| journal = Chem. Phys. Lett.| year = 2008| volume = 451| issue = 1–3 | pages = 88–92 | bibcode = 2008CPL...451...88Y }}</ref> establishing a world record; however, some scholars questioned the assumptions of that study.<ref>{{cite journal | author1 = Caupin, F. | author2 = Herbert, E. | author3 = Balibar, S. | author4 = Cole, M. W. | title = Comment on 'Nanoscale water capillary bridges under deeply negative pressure' (Chem. Phys. Lett. 451 (2008) 88) |doi=10.1016/j.cplett.2008.08.047| journal = Chem. Phys. Lett.| year = 2008| volume = 463| issue = 1–3 | pages = 283–285 | bibcode = 2008CPL...463..283C }}</ref>  

Among other results obtained during his tenure at the [[University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee]] are the observation of wetting transitions in underwater oleophobic metallic surfaces,<ref>{{cite journal | author1 = Hejazi, V. | author2 = Nyong, A. E. | author3 = Rohatgi, P.K. | author4 = Nosonovsky, M. | title = Wetting transitions in underwater oleophobic surface of brass |doi=10.1002/adma.201202516| journal = Advanced Materials| year = 2012| volume = 24| issue = 44 | pages = 5963–5966 | pmid = 22945753 | bibcode = 2012AdM....24.5963H }}</ref> an explanation of why hydrophobic materials do not always repel ice,<ref>[https://www.scientificamerican.com/blog/assignment-impossible/worth-pitching-mysteries-of-rain-and-ice/ Charles Q. Choi, Mysteries of Rain and Ice (Scientific American blogs, October 5, 2012)]</ref> the application of [[Non-equilibrium thermodynamics]] to the study of [[Self-healing material]], supehydrophobic concrete and antimicrobial coatings,<ref>[https://uwm.edu/engineering/uwm-researchers-develop-spray-on-coating-that-repels-deactivates-airborne-pathogens/ UWM researchers develop spray-on coating that repels, deactivates airborne pathogens]</ref> and the application of the separation of motions method, which is used in mechanics for the studies of [[Kapitza's pendulum]], to the problems of surface physics and chemistry.<ref>{{cite journal | author1 = Hasan, M.S. | author2 = Nosonovsky, M. | title = Method of separation of vibrational motions for applications involving wetting, superhydrophobicity, and microparticle extraction |doi=10.1103/PhysRevFluids.5.054201| journal = Physical Review Fluids| year = 2020| volume = 5| issue = 5 | article-number = 054201 | bibcode = 2020PhRvF...5e4201H }}</ref>   

In 2010, Nosonovsky, together with [[Bharat Bhushan (academic)|Bharat Bhushan]] suggested 12 principles of a new scientific discipline, Green [[Tribology]] (or Ecotribology),<ref>{{cite journal | author1 = Nosonovsky, M. | author2 = Bhushan, B. | title = Green tribology: principles, research areas and challenges |doi=10.1098/rsta.2010.0200 | journal = Phil. Trans. Royal Soc. A | year = 2010| volume = 368 | issue = 1929 | pages = 4677–4694 | pmid = 20855315 | bibcode = 2010RSPTA.368.4677N }}</ref> which are now widely used by researchers in various parts of the world.<ref>{{cite journal | author1 = Freschi, M. | title = The Twelve Principles of Green Tribology: Studies, Research, and Case Studies — A Brief Anthology |doi=10.3390/lubricants10060129| journal = Lubricants| year = 2022| volume = 10| issue = 6 | pages = 129 | doi-access = free }}</ref> Nosonovsky was also a pioneer of another new scientific discipline, Triboinformatics.<ref>[https://uwm.edu/engineering/nosonovsky-pioneer-in-the-science-of-triboinformatics-promoted-to-professor-at-uwm/ Nosonovsky, pioneer in the science of triboinformatics, promoted to professor at UWM]</ref>    

Among other topics, Nosonovsky's research projects included investigations of mechanisms of wringing in [[Gauge block| Johansson Gauge blocks]],<ref>{{cite journal | author1 = Breki, A.| author2 = Nosonovsky, M.| title = Friction and adhesion of Johansson gauge blocks |doi=10.1680/jsuin.22.01083| journal = Surface Innovations| year = 2024| volume = 12| issue = 1–2 | pages = 18–22}}</ref> investigating the lowest possible surface energy of a solid,<ref>{{cite journal | author1 = Chen, Z.| author2 = Nosonovsky, M.| title = Revisiting lowest possible surface energy of a solid |doi=10.1088/2051-672X/aa84c9| journal = Surface Topography: Metrology and Properties| year = 2017| volume = 5| issue = 4 | pages = 045001| bibcode = 2017SuTMP...5d5001C}}</ref> and understanding the role of friction in the invention of the pendulum clock.<ref>{{cite journal | author1 = Blumenthal, A. S.| author2 = Nosonovsky, M.| title = Friction and dynamics of verge and foliot: How the invention of the pendulum made clocks much more accurate |doi=10.3390/applmech1020008| journal = Applied Mechanics| year = 2020| volume = 1| issue = 2 | pages = 111–121 | doi-access = free }}</ref> Since 2017, Nosonovsky studied various aspects of the levitating [[Droplet cluster]] including the applicability of [[Dynkin diagram]] and [[ADE classification]] to the diversity of small clusters.<ref>{{cite journal | author1 = Fedorets, A.| author2 = Bormashenko, E. | author3 = Dombrovsky, L.| author4 = Nosonovsky, M.| title = Symmetry of small clusters of levitating water droplets |doi=10.1039/D0CP01804J | journal = Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys.| year = 2020| volume = 22 | issue = 21 | pages = 12239–12244 | pmid = 32432244 | bibcode = 2020PCCP...2212239F }}</ref>

During his tenure as ITMO Fellow in the [https://en.itmo.ru/en/department/489/Infochemistry_Scientific_Center.htm Infochemistry Scientific Center] at [[ITMO University]], Nosonovsky investigated new methods of surface roughness analysis, such as [[Topological data analysis]], and applications of Triboinformatics to various areas<ref>[https://news.itmo.ru/en/news/12269/ ITMO Fellowship & Professorship Participants Discuss Their Research Projects]</ref> ranging from taste studies<ref>{{cite journal | author1 = Shityakov, S. | title = TAS2R taste receptor clustering suggests that bitter wine taste perception forms a 2D dataspace |doi=10.1142/S2737416524500844| journal = J. Comput. Biophys. Chem.| year = 2025| volume = 24| issue = 6 | pages = 795–805 | bibcode = 2025JCBC...24..795S }}</ref> to protein folding,<ref>[https://news.itmo.ru/en/news/12801/ T. Besedina. ITMO Scientists Discover Universal Measure to Predict Protein Folding.]</ref> to applications of [[Ergodicity]] to cancer treatment.<ref>{{cite journal | author1 = Shityakov, S. | title = Ergodicity Breaking and Self-Destruction of Cancer Cells by Induced Genome Chaos |doi=10.3390/e26010037| journal = Entropy| year = 2024| volume = 26| issue = 1 | pages = 37 | pmid = 38248163 | pmc = 10814486 | doi-access = free }}</ref> 

Besides his work in mechanical engineering, materials science, and chemistry, Nosonovsky has several important academic publications in the field of history including [[History of science]],<ref>{{cite journal | author1 = Nosonovsky, M | title = Oil as a Lubricant in the Ancient Middle East |doi=10.2474/trol.2.44| journal = Tribology Online| year = 2007| volume = 2| issue = 2 | pages = 4-49}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | author1 = Nosonovsky, M | title = Early Renaissance Concepts of Time and the Invention of Mechanical Clocks |doi=10.32388/TNV08C| journal = Qeios| year = 2024}}</ref> and [[Hebrew]] [[Epigraphy]].<ref>{{cite journal | author1 = Fishel, A | author2 = Nosonovsky, M | title = The structure of Karaite gravestone inscriptions from Çufut-Qal‘eh and methodology of Hebrew Epigraphy | doi=10.24411/2713-2021-2020-00030| journal = Proceedings in Archaeology and History of Ancient and Medieval Black Sea Region| year = 2020| volume = 12| issue = 20 | pages = 996-1014}}</ref>  This includes the catalog of 16th-century Jewish gravestones in Ukraine<ref>[https://www.academia.edu/12269862/%D0%AD%D0%BF%D0%B8%D1%82%D0%B0%D1%84%D0%B8%D0%B8_XVI_%D0%B2_%D1%81_%D0%B5%D0%B2%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%B9%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B8%D1%85_%D0%BD%D0%B0%D0%B4%D0%B3%D1%80%D0%BE%D0%B1%D0%B8%D0%B9_%D0%A3%D0%BA%D1%80%D0%B0%D0%B8%D0%BD%D1%8B_The_16th_century_epitaphs_on_Jewish_gravestones_in_Ukraine  The 16th century epitaphs on Jewish gravestones in Ukraine]</ref> with the oldest gravestones from the region,<ref>{{cite journal | author1 = Fishel, A. | author2 = Nosonovsky, M. | title = Rediscovered Gravestones from a Destroyed Jewish Cemetery in Ostróg: The Case of Two Inscriptions of 1445 |doi=10.1163/18750214-12141058| journal = Zutot| year = 2017| volume = 14 | pages = 73–87 }}</ref> the identification and publication of the first Hebrew book in Central Asia,<ref>[https://www.academia.edu/39493085/A_Bukharan_Jewish_Judeo_Tajik_translation_of_the_1001_Nights_Arabian_Nights_published_in_Kokand_X%C3%B6kand_Qoqon_in_1914 A Bukharan-Jewish (Judeo-Tajik) translation of the "1001 Nights" ("Arabian Nights") published in Kokand (Xökand / Qo'qon) in 1914]</ref> identification and publication of a 17th century [[Crimean Karaites|Karaite]] poem from [[Derazhne]],<ref>{{cite journal | author = Nosonovsky, M. | title = The Karaite Community in Derażne and its Leader Hazzan Joseph ben Yeshu'ah | journal = Eastern European Karaites in the Last Generations| year = 2011| pages = 17–35}}</ref> finding the oldest gravestone with a Hebrew inscription in Belarus,<ref>[https://www.facebook.com/esjff/posts/have-we-found-the-oldest-matzevah-in-belarusas-part-of-the-esjf-national-survey-/1966656620242778/ ESJF European Jewish Cemeteries Initiative-Have we found the oldest matzevah in Belarus?]</ref> the identification of the gravestone of [[Josiah Pardo]], the first Rabbi in Central / North America in [[Kingston, Jamaica]],<ref name=Nos1>{{Citation
 | last = Nosonovsky
 | first = M
 | title = New Findings at the Old Jewish Cemetery of Hunts Bay, Jamaica
 | place = Moscow - Jerusalem
 | publisher = Gesharim
 | series = Studia Anthlopoligica
 | year = 2010
 | pages = 116–118
 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=YXRsAgAAQBAJ
 | isbn = 978-5-93273-319-6}}</ref> the identification of the oldest synagogue in Morocco,<ref>{{cite journal | author1 = Andreeva, S. | author2 = Fedorchuk, A. | author3 = Nosonovsky, M. | title = Revisiting Epigraphic Evidence of the Oldest Synagogue in Morocco in Volubilis |doi=10.3390/arts8040127| journal = Arts| year = 2019| volume = 8| issue = 4 | pages = 127 | doi-access = free }}</ref> and establishing the role of [[Abner of Burgos]] in the development of the Copernicus astronomic system.<ref>{{cite journal | author1 = Nosonovsky, M. | title = Abner of Burgos: The Missing Link between Nasir al-Din al-Tusi and Nicolaus Copernicus? |doi=10.1163/18750214-12151070| journal = Zutot| year = 2018| volume = 15 | pages = 25–30 }}</ref> Nosonovsky also has academic publications on the Afro-Cuban religion of [[Santería]] / [[Ifá]].<ref>{{cite journal | author1 = Nosonovsky, M. | title = Translation or Divination? Sacred Languages and Bilingualism in Judaism and Lucumí Traditions |doi=10.3390/rel13010057| journal = Religions| year = 2022| volume = 13| issue = 1 | pages = 57 | doi-access = free }}</ref>

== Honors and achievements ==
Nosonovsky has coauthored and edited nine books, including the first monograph on biomimetic self-healing materials,<ref>{{cite book |last1=Nosonovsky |first1=M. |last2=Rohatgi |first2=P. |date=2011 |title=Biomimetics in Materials Science: Self-healing, self-lubricating, and self-cleaning materials |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cmmQBsZvxp4C&pg=PR7 |location=New York |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-1-4614-0925-0 }}</ref> a monograph on [[Droplet cluster]]<ref>{{cite book |last1=Fedorets |first1=A. |last2=Dombrovsky |first2=L. |last3=Bormashenko |first3=E. |last4=Nosonovsky |first4=M. |date=2024 |title=Levitating Droplet Clusters |url=https://www.begellhouse.com/books/7a8b7dac4dc1df3b.html |location=New York |publisher=Begell House |isbn=
978-1-56700-532-5}}</ref> and more than 200 peer-reviewed research articles.<ref>[https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=Ct5Kv-UAAAAJ&hl=en M. Nosonovsky on Google Scholar]</ref> He is a recipient of the [[ASME Burt L. Newkirk Award]] "for outstanding research in nanotribology, adhesion, and tribology of functional bioinspired surfaces, including the scale effect on friction and patterned nonadhesive surfaces using the Lotus effect."<ref>[https://www.asme.org/about-asme/honors-awards/achievement-awards/burt-l-newkirk-award ASME Burt Newkirk Award]</ref> He was also a recipient of the UWM Foundation Research Award.<ref>[https://uwm.edu/officeofresearch/ords/research-recognition-awards/past-research-recognition-awardees/ Research Recognition Awardees]</ref>
